# Altair: group meetups slice First Epic workflow challenge (Senior Full-Stack, Altair). This repo has: - the database and its access rules (Supabase/Postgres) - one write endpoint (a Supabase Edge Function) - one shared Zod contract - access tests - the React Native app (Expo, Android) It also has both bonus parts: meetup editing, and a live-map sample. - **Note** (decisions, what I directed and caught, pushback): [docs/NOTE.md](docs/NOTE.md) - **Decision records:** [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) - **Live map latency / battery / load-test note:** [docs/live-map-note.md](docs/live-map-note.md) - **AI session logs:** [ai-logs/](ai-logs/) ## Repository layout ``` supabase/migrations/ starter schema + timestamped migrations (tables, RLS/grants, write functions, bonus) supabase/seed.sql seed PART 1 (accounts, groups) + PART 2 adapted to this schema supabase/functions/ meetups Edge Function: POST/PATCH/DELETE writes, validated with the shared contract packages/contracts/ the shared Zod schemas, imported by the Edge Function (Deno) and the app (Metro) tests/ Vitest access tests against the local stack (real Auth sessions, real API) apps/mobile/ Expo SDK 58 app (Expo Router, react-native-maps) tools/live-sim.ts bonus (b): simulated live positions + load probe ``` ## Prerequisites - **Node.js 24** (tested with 24.21; `tools/live-sim.ts` relies on Node's built-in TypeScript support). - **Docker Desktop**, running. - To run the app, either: - an **Android phone** with **Expo Go** from the Play Store, or - an **Android emulator** with Google Play (Android Studio), which also has Expo Go. Only Android was tested. No accounts, API keys or map keys are needed. Everything runs locally. ## Run it from a clean checkout All commands run from the repo root unless a step says otherwise. Keep one terminal per long-running process. ### 1. Install ``` npm install ``` This also installs the Supabase CLI as a dev dependency, so use `npx supabase ...`. ### 2. Database: migrations and seed ``` npx supabase start npx supabase db reset ``` `start` pulls the Docker images on first run (a few minutes) and boots the stack. `db reset` applies every migration in `supabase/migrations/` in order, then `supabase/seed.sql`: - PART 1: the seed accounts and groups - PART 2: the three reference meetups and their RSVPs Run `db reset` any time you want a clean database. `npx supabase status` prints the URLs and the local keys. Studio, the database UI, is at http://127.0.0.1:54323. ### 3. Write endpoint (terminal A, keep it open) ``` npx supabase functions serve ``` It serves `http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/meetups`. If you restart the stack, start this again. ### 4. Tests (terminal B) ``` npm test ``` 63 tests run against the local stack. Each signs in as a seed persona through Supabase Auth and calls the real API. If a database reset has just finished, the first run waits a few seconds for Realtime. The tests are re-runnable without a reset. | File | Proves | |---|---| | `read-access.test.ts` | The four roles on "Saturday morning loop":
• Taylor, the outsider, reads nothing: meetup, attendees, meeting point or groups.
• Sam, no RSVP, gets an approximate area ≥ 300 m, not centered on the exact point, with no place name.
• Jordan (RSVP'd) and Avery (creator) see the exact point.
• Signed-out requests are denied. | | `multi-group.test.ts` | Riley (both groups): map data follows Riley's own status per meetup, and an RSVP to one meetup unlocks nothing else. Single-group members see only their own group. | | `writes.test.ts` | Future-start rule; strict input; **creator-only cancel**; **no RSVP to a cancelled meetup** or a started one (set up as DB owner); cancelling is final; withdraw after cancel; RSVP is idempotent | | `bypass.test.ts` | Direct table writes and direct calls to the write functions with a user session are denied. `home_lat`/`home_lng` are unreadable for everyone. | | `edit.test.ts` | Bonus (a): creator-only edit, future-start re-check, no edit after cancel, new approximate area when the point moves | | `live.test.ts` | Bonus (b): only group members can join or send on the group's private Realtime channel | | *(every file)* | Every response body is scanned for all seeded home coordinates | ### 5. The app (terminal C) Create the app's env file. It holds the local API URL and the public local anon key. Never put the service role key in it. ``` # PowerShell Copy-Item apps/mobile/.env.example apps/mobile/.env # macOS / Linux cp apps/mobile/.env.example apps/mobile/.env ``` Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` in `apps/mobile/.env` to match how the device reaches your computer: | Device | URL | Extra step | |---|---|---| | Phone over Wi-Fi | `http://:54321`, e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:54321` | Same Wi-Fi network. On Windows: set the network profile to **Private**, and allow inbound TCP 8081 (Expo) and 54321 (Supabase). See below. | | Phone over USB | `http://127.0.0.1:54321` | `adb reverse tcp:54321 tcp:54321` and `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` (details in [docs/run-on-phone.md](docs/run-on-phone.md)) | | Android emulator | `http://10.0.2.2:54321` | none | Then start the app: ``` cd apps/mobile npx expo start --clear ``` - **Phone:** in **Expo Go**, use *Scan QR code* (inside Expo Go, not the camera app) on the terminal's QR code, or *Enter URL manually*: `exp://:8081`. - **Emulator:** press `a`. Use `--clear` whenever you change `.env`; Expo bakes those values in at bundle time. **Sign in** with a seed account. The sign-in screen has one-tap buttons for them. Every password is `altair-fixture-pass`. | Account | Role | |---|---| | `avery@example.test` | Maple Street Walkers; creator of "Saturday morning loop" | | `jordan@example.test` | Maple; RSVP'd to Saturday; creator of "Weeknight short walk" | | `sam@example.test` | Maple; no RSVPs | | `riley@example.test` | **Both groups**; RSVP'd to Saturday only | | `morgan@example.test` | Riverside Loop Walkers; creator of "Riverside sunrise walk" | | `casey@example.test` | Riverside; RSVP'd to Riverside sunrise walk | | `quinn@example.test` | Riverside; no RSVPs | | `taylor@example.test` | **Outsider**: in no group | **Quick walkthrough:** 1. Sign in as **Sam** and open *Saturday morning loop*. The map shows an approximate **circle** and no place name. 2. Tap **RSVP**. The map becomes a **pin** at *North gate, Linden Park*. 3. Sign in as **Taylor**. You get the "not in any walking groups" empty state. 4. Sign in as **Avery**. *Saturday morning loop* shows **Edit** and **Cancel**, which only the creator sees. ### 6. Bonus (b): live map (terminal D, optional) ``` npm run live-sim ``` This broadcasts 25 **simulated** walkers on Maple Street Walkers' private channel. In the app, as a Maple member such as Sam, tap **Live map (demo)**. Zoom in to see culling: "known" stays the same while "rendered" drops. As Morgan, a non-member, the screen says you're not a member. To run it as a load probe: ``` npm run live-sim -- --walkers 80 --clients 1 --measure --duration 30 ``` Local Realtime caps a project at 100 events/s. See [docs/live-map-note.md](docs/live-map-note.md) before going higher. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Fix | |---|---| | `docker: command not found` from `npx supabase ...` (Windows) | Docker Desktop's `resources\bin` isn't on this terminal's PATH. Open a new terminal; if VS Code started before Docker was installed, sign out and back in to Windows. | | App: "Can't reach the server", or Expo Go can't connect | On the phone's browser, open `http://:8081/status`. If it doesn't load: check the same Wi-Fi, a Private network profile, and the firewall rule below. | | Writes fail (create, RSVP, cancel) but lists load | `npx supabase functions serve` isn't running. Start it (step 3). | | Live map stays "Connecting…" | Realtime starts a few seconds after the rest of the stack; wait and reopen the screen. | | `.env` change has no effect | Restart Expo with `--clear`. | Windows firewall rule for Wi-Fi testing (admin PowerShell; Private networks only): ``` New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Altair dev (Expo 8081 + Supabase 54321)" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8081,54321 -Action Allow -Profile Private ``` ## Endpoints All writes go through one Edge Function. The user is taken from the `Authorization: Bearer` token, never from the body. Bodies are validated with the shared schemas in `packages/contracts`. | Method | Path | Body | Success | |---|---|---|---| | POST | `/functions/v1/meetups` | `CreateMeetupInput` | 201 `{ id }` | | PATCH | `/functions/v1/meetups/:id` | `UpdateMeetupInput` (bonus) | 200 `{ id }` | | POST | `/functions/v1/meetups/:id/cancel` | none | 200 `{ id, status: "cancelled" }` | | POST | `/functions/v1/meetups/:id/rsvp` | none | 200 `{ meetupId, attending: true }` | | DELETE | `/functions/v1/meetups/:id/rsvp` | none | 200 `{ meetupId, attending: false }` | Errors use `{ error: { code, message, issues? } }`: - 400 `invalid_input` - 401 `unauthorized` - 403 `forbidden` (a member who isn't the creator) - 404 `not_found` (also returned to outsiders, so existence never leaks) - 409 `conflict` (cancelled or started) Reads go straight to `meetup_details`, `meetup_attendees` and `groups` with the user's session, under RLS.

# Recording plan (10–15 min) — personal, not committed

The brief: "explains *why*, not a click tour". It must include:
- a live run of the slice
- the map before and after an RSVP
- an outsider who can't read the meetup or its attendees

Speak in your own words: these are cues, not a script. Imperfect delivery is fine, so don't
re-record for polish.

## Before you hit record (5 min)
- [ ] Close Chrome tabs, TradingView, and anything unrelated. Phone on **Do Not Disturb**.
- [ ] Docker running. `npx supabase db reset` for a clean seed (Sam has no RSVP).
- [ ] Terminal A: `npx supabase functions serve` (live logs visible).
- [ ] Terminal B: `cd apps\mobile` then `npx expo start --clear`. The app is open on the Pixel
      and signed out.
- [ ] Terminal C at the repo root, ready for `npm test`, `npm run outsider-demo`, `npm run live-sim`.
- [ ] Google Meet joined from laptop and Pixel, Pixel sharing its screen, Pixel tile pinned.
- [ ] VS Code tabs open: `supabase/migrations/20261027120100_access.sql`,
      `packages/contracts/src/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/meetups/index.ts`, `docs/NOTE.md`.
- [ ] Recorder set to the whole screen, with the mic on.

## 1. What this is (≈1 min)
- The slice: DB + endpoint + shared contract + RN app; built with Claude Code, and I directed the calls.
- One sentence on the core idea: **the database is the boundary.** Anything the app could
  hide, an attacker with the anon key can ask for directly, so the app hides nothing.

## 2. Access model: why it's built this way (≈3 min) — show `access.sql`
- RLS filters **rows**, not columns. Both privacy rules are about *part* of a row.
- **The split table:** the exact place lives in `meetup_meeting_points`, readable only by the
  creator or an attendee. That's why the map changes after RSVP with no special code.
- **The column grant:** `users` exposes only `(id, display_name)`, so `home_lat` gives
  permission denied for everyone.
- **Caught:** Supabase grants ALL to anon/authenticated by default; I revoke it.
- **Writes:** no write grants, and the write functions are service_role only, so the endpoint
  is the only way in. Show `index.ts`: user id from the JWT, then `parse(Schema)`, then the RPC.
- Show `contracts/index.ts`: one file imported by Deno and Metro. `strictObject` rejects
  `createdBy`. One shared future-start rule.

## 3. Live run on the phone (≈3–4 min)
1. **Sam** → *Saturday morning loop*: **a circle and no place name**. Say why: 500 m, center
   offset 100–450 m, stored once. Mention the fixed flaw (the first plan's ring was too narrow).
2. Tap **RSVP** → **a pin at North gate, Linden Park**. Point at Terminal A logs (the POST).
   Explain: it's the same query, but the meeting-point row now comes back.
3. (Optional) Withdraw → the circle again.
4. **Create** a meetup with a past time → the error under the date (shared schema). Then a valid
   one → it opens with the exact pin (Sam is its creator).
5. **Avery** → Saturday: **Edit** and **Cancel** appear only for the creator. Cancel it → shown
   as cancelled. **Sam** → the RSVP button is gone. (Optional) Show the API returning 409.
6. **Riley** (both groups): exact for Saturday, approximate for the others. That's the
   multi-group case.

## 4. Outsider (≈1.5 min)
- **Taylor** in the app: "not in any walking groups".
- Terminal C: `npm run outsider-demo` → Taylor gets `[]` for the meetup, attendees and point,
  and a **404** from the endpoint (not 403, so existence doesn't leak). Sam, for contrast, gets
  approximate only. Both are denied `home_lat` and direct inserts.

## 5. Tests (≈1 min)
- `npm test` → 63 pass. While it runs, name what they prove: the four roles, creator-only
  cancel, no RSVP to cancelled or started meetups (set up as owner), multi-group map data,
  direct writes denied, and a home-coordinate scan of every response.
- Mention the test that failed for the right reason (Sam as a creator) and the Realtime timing
  fix.

## 6. Bonus (≈1.5 min)
- Edit: re-saving the same point **doesn't** create a new circle (averaging attack).
- `npm run live-sim` → **Live map (demo)** as Sam. Zoom in: "rendered" drops and "known"
  stays (culling). Movement is smooth (1.2 s interpolation buffer).
- The finding: over 100 events/s, Realtime **drops silently** while `send()` says ok, so
  measure at the receiver. Plus my wrong first guess (fan-out), which a run disproved.
- Simulated positions only, on purpose (see refuse-first).

## 7. Judgment (≈2 min) — `NOTE.md` on screen
- **Product call:** approximate until RSVP. Give the reason in your words, plus the honest limit
  (RSVP and withdraw).
- **Refuse first:** anything derived from home location (it can be trilaterated).
- **Pushback:** the weak RSVP gate; home location in the profile table; edits silently changing
  what people RSVP'd to; the attendee list before RSVP.
- **Not reached:** iOS not run; no UI tests; hosted path not exercised; live map not profiled.
- **AI use:** Claude Code. The log is in `ai-logs/`. Where I pushed back: the one-function
  change.

**Total ≈ 13–14 min.** If you're running long, shorten section 6.
